integrity: Analytic proof reconstructs the finite Blaschke factorization, rational phase-derivative identity, degenerate stationary phase, and lower bound on product degree. Standard-library exact identities and finite quadrature are corroborative, not substitutes for infinite arguments. The novelty assessment is based on accessible published comparisons and may not encompass undiscovered work.
scientific_limitations: Theorem is confined to the seventh-order exponent and one explicit degree-three product; the coefficient asymptotic is for the frequency 7n, whereas only two-sided order bounds are asserted for the supremum. Other exponents, uniqueness, and exact supremum constants are not settled.
title: A degree-three Blaschke product realizes the seventh-order Fourier exponent optimally
